nodes.label: W-254 — I asked for a ruling that was already in §6.1
nodes.rationale: M: 'you have to read for context to know.' W-252 called the operator question subject matter needing a ruling; it needed a reading.

nodes.label: ℛ — the (≤,≤) corner closure, from three agreeing places
nodes.rationale: §6.1 defines the value sets, the monotone envelope φ̂ᵢⱼ(v) = max{xᵢ : x ∈ X, xⱼ ≤ v} and ℛ; the glossary names ℛ₄ as the closure over all four orientations and E − E₄ as the orientation cost. So §14.5.3's two pairwise operators are ℛ and ℛ₄ — neither is the raw two-dimensional projection.

nodes.label: bundling.py implemented an operator the book does not have
nodes.rationale: Its ℛ was 'every tuple whose every 2-D projection lies in X's', with no monotone envelope anywhere in it — under which ℛ(X) = X at two coordinates is trivially true, which is where register 1848's general reason came from. Left in place because it is what produced 1848.

nodes.label: bundling2.py — validated against the book's own printed number
nodes.rationale: §6.1 says the periodic table's E is 36 and the successor returns 36. The check that should have settled it at once: an implementation of ℛ that cannot return 36 for the periodic table is not ℛ.

nodes.label: Register 1853 — 1852 superseded
nodes.rationale: A seated correction can be wrong, and the append-only mechanic is what makes that survivable: 1852 stands in the record with 1853 citing it, exactly as DEFERRED.md's CORRECTION-SUPERSEDED class anticipated.

nodes.label: An envelope keyed on equality instead of ≤
nodes.rationale: The first measurement used max{xᵢ : xⱼ = v} where §6.1 writes xⱼ ≤ v — per-value rather than cumulative. On the three cells that one difference is the whole finding: equality gives E = 1 and ≤ gives E = 2, and the re-derivation that reported E = 2 was right for the reason it gave.

nodes.label: §14.3's own qualifier survives every correction
nodes.rationale: Bundling does hide a defect (2 → 0 under ℛ, 1 → 0 under ℛ₄), and only one of the three folds closes — so the operative condition is the chapter's own 'folding into one non-chain coordinate'. The chapter was more careful than the register entry that set out to correct it.
